answer: The fable multiplier is published, charged in thread, and falcon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 20 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4941 identities would post 3329 proofs and burn roughly 3 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
